items.question: What attainment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginis?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation constitute a great accomplishment
Such accomplishment can belong to a practitioner
Possessing it makes one dear to the yoginis
items.inference: A practitioner endowed with the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginis.
items.plain_english: One who attains the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginis.

rows.grounds: locative participle indicating context of emergence

premises: A teaching has emerged in Candra-dvipa
A chapter is identified by ordinal number

items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes in the context of what emerged in Candra-dvipa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, which emerged in Candra-dvipa.

items.plain_english: One should visualize oneself surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What request acknowledges the revelation of knowledge's determination?

items.plain_english: O God, today the determination of knowledge has been made manifest to me.

items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell me how the secret place, as a wheel, brings swift accomplishment.

items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O Great Goddess! You have asked me about something that is hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ located in the subtle body?

uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form; taken as the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is at the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.plain_english: O Goddess, in brief, one attains immortality and likewise transformation.
